paragraphs.text: Avery Delgado is a 15-year-old female followed by child and adolescent psychiatry for recurrent major depressive disorder (moderate), generalized anxiety disorder, and combined-type ADHD diagnosed at age 9.
She had an inpatient psychiatric admission for suicidal ideation in December 2025.
paragraphs.kind: Fabrication (no admission anywhere in the chart)

paragraphs.text: Her problem list also includes generalized anxiety disorder and a history of nonsuicidal self-injury, with the last episode in February 2026.
Family history is notable for bipolar I disorder in her father, with no known family history of suicide.
paragraphs.kind: Misattribution (the aunt's diagnosis given to the father)
paragraphs.claude_text: Family history is notable for a maternal aunt with bipolar I disorder and a father with ADHD, with no known family history of suicide.

paragraphs.text: In June 2026 her depression was moderately severe with partial response to sertraline (PHQ-A 16, GAD-7 13), so sertraline was increased from 50 mg to 75 mg daily.
Two weeks later she had slightly better mornings but persistent evening irritability, rapid mood shifts, and explosive arguments at home without physical aggression.
Given persistent mood lability and the family history of bipolar disorder, off-label adjunctive lamotrigine 25 mg daily was started on 06/24/2026 with rash counseling.

On day 15 of lamotrigine she presented to the ED with a pruritic maculopapular rash on the chest, back, and upper arms, diagnosed as a benign morbilliform drug eruption without features of Stevens-Johnson syndrome or DRESS.
Two days later she returned to the ED with a fever and a rapidly spreading rash, and lamotrigine was permanently discontinued and added to her allergy list.
paragraphs.kind: Confabulation (a return precaution turned into an event)
paragraphs.claude_text: Lamotrigine was stopped, the rash resolved without fever, blistering, or mouth sores, and it was permanently discontinued and added to her allergy list with no plan to rechallenge.

paragraphs.text: At her 09/16/2026 visit, mood was improved with fewer home arguments, and she has attended full days of 10th grade without absences.
PHQ-A improved to 9 (mild) from 16 in June, and GAD-7 improved to 8 (mild).
Her suicidal ideation has resolved, and she denies self-harm since February.
paragraphs.kind: Overstatement (passive SI a couple of times this month)
paragraphs.claude_text: She reports fleeting passive suicidal ideation a couple of times in the past month without plan or intent and denies self-harm since February.

paragraphs.text: In August therapy she resisted a strong urge to self-harm after a peer conflict by using the TIPP skill, and her safety plan was reviewed.
Her mother has confirmed there are no firearms in the home and that medications are kept in a locked box.
paragraphs.kind: Mis-citation (true, but the therapy note doesn't say it; N1.9 does)
paragraphs.claude_text: Her mother has confirmed there are no firearms in the home and that medications are kept in a locked box.

paragraphs.text: June fatigue labs showed normal TSH, free T4, and hemoglobin, but low ferritin at 11 ng/mL and low 25-OH vitamin D at 17 ng/mL.
A February 2026 right-hand X-ray after she punched a wall showed no fracture, only soft-tissue swelling over the fifth knuckle.
paragraphs.kind: Added accurate sentence (so imaging is represented)

paragraphs.text: Ferrous sulfate 325 mg every other day and vitamin D3 2,000 IU daily were started on 09/16/2026, and weight was up 2.1 kg since June.
Sertraline was increased to 100 mg daily at the September visit, and guanfacine ER 2 mg and melatonin 3 mg nightly continue.
paragraphs.kind: Plan stated as done (100 mg was only to be considered)
paragraphs.claude_text: The plan is to continue sertraline 75 mg daily with a possible increase to 100 mg if improvement plateaus, plus guanfacine ER 2 mg and melatonin 3 mg nightly.

paragraphs.text: No mood stabilizer is planned for now given her improvement, weekly therapy continues, and she returns in 4 weeks.
